label: A4
title: Everyday Tagalog expressions
summary: Ready-made phrases for directions, children, time, speaking Tagalog, introductions, dressing up, parties, goodbyes, the market, kitchen, dining room and living room
goals: Ask for places and directions, and get around by bus or taxi
Say the day, month, date and year
Tell people you are learning Tagalog and ask for help
Use polite phrases as a guest or host: at a party, at meals, in the living room and when saying goodbye
Shop at the market and talk about the kitchen

blocks.t: Lesson 3 gave you the first everyday expressions: greetings such as *Good day*, *How are you* and *Excuse me*, and the respect word **pô**. This appendix adds more ready-made phrases, grouped by **place or situation** (the market, the kitchen…), plus **instructions for children**. They are the kind of phrases you need when you talk with native Tagalog speakers.

blocks.title: How to use this lesson
items: Learn each phrase as a whole, like a block. You do not need to take every word apart.
Tap **Listen** on the examples and say them out loud.
Notice the respect word **pô / po** (Lesson 3) and the request words starting with **paki-** (Lesson 24), such as **Pakiturò** (please show) and **Paki-úlit** (please repeat).
Commands with **Huwág** (*do not*) come from Lesson 37.

blocks.t: Phrases for finding places, asking for directions and taking a bus or taxi. **Saán** (*where*) starts many of them.

items.tl: Saán akó makakakíta ng isáng magalíng na réstawran?
items.en: Where can I find a good restaurant?

items.tl: Saán akó makakakíta ng simbáhang Protestánte?
items.en: Where can I find a Protestant church?
Where can I find a doctor?

items.tl: Anó ang pangálan ng kalsádang itó?
items.en: What is the name of this street?

items.tl: Gaáno katagal ang datíng ng (súsunod na) bus?
items.en: How long before the (next) bus comes?

items.tl: Saán páparoón ang bus na itó?
Anóng oras ang datíng nitóng bus sa Maynilà?
items.en: What time does this bus arrive in Manila?

items.tl: Paáno pumuntá sa Ortigas Avenue mulâ ditó?
items.en: How do I get to Ortigas Avenue from here?

items.tl: Anó ang ngálan ng báryong itó?
items.en: What is the name of this barrio?

items.tl: Puwéde bang inumín ang túbig na itó?
items.en: Is this water safe to drink?

blocks.title: Stopping a ride
blocks.t: **Pára po!** is what you call out to make a jeepney or bus stop. Add **sa kánto** to say *at the corner*.

blocks.title: Book spellings
items: This page prints **Gaáno katagal**; page 199 prints **Gáano katagál**.

blocks.t: Short commands for children. Several begin with **Huwág** (*do not*), followed by **kang**, **kayóng** or **mong** (ka, kayó, mo + the ligature -ng from Lesson 7).

items.tl: Maghúgas ka ng kamáy at mukhâ.
Isuót mo ang iyóng sapatos at damít.
items.en: Put on your shoes and clothes.

items.tl: Iligpít mo ang iyóng mga laruán.

items.en: Do not wake up the baby.

blocks.title: Do not…
items: **Huwág mong gisíngin ang sanggól.** Do not wake up the baby.

blocks.t: Saying the time, day, month, date and year. The book writes the date as **ika-20 (or a bente)** and the year 2007 as **dalawáng libo at pitó**.

items.tl: Ang pétsa ay ika-20 (or a bente) ng Abríl.
Ang taón ay dalawáng libo at pitó.

blocks.t: Useful phrases while you are learning: tell people you are learning, ask them to repeat or to correct you.

items.en: I am learning to speak Tagalog.
Please talk to me in Tagalog.
How do you say ... in Tagalog?

blocks.title: Asking for a word
blocks.t: **Paáno sinásabi sa Tagálog ang ... ?** Put the English word in the gap: *How do you say ... in Tagalog?*
Giving your name, asking someone's name and introducing a friend.

items.tl: Itó ang kaibígan kong si Paolo.

items.en: I am pleased to meet you.

items.tl: Ikáw ba ang kaibígan ng kapatíd kong babáe?

blocks.title: Book spellings
blocks.t: Page 198 prints **Hindí kitá kilalá** with an acute accent on hindí; page 197 prints **Hindî ko maintindihán**.
Talking about what to wear.

items.tl: Ewan ko. Walá akóng bágong damít.
items.en: I do not know. I don't have a new dress.

items.tl: Isúsuót ko ang áking Bárong Tagálog.
items.en: I will wear my Barong Tagalog.

blocks.title: Barong Tagalog and amérikana
blocks.t: **Amérikana** refers to the formal coat and tie introduced by the Americans. A coat is warm (**Maínit ang amérikana**), while the Barong Tagalog is cool to wear (**Itó ay malamíg isuót**).
Phrases a host and a guest use when food is served.

items.tl: Handâ na ang pagkain. Kumáin na táyo.
items.en: The food is ready. Let's eat.
Thank you. I am already full.
Thank you. I am already full. (the book's other way to say it)

blocks.title: Don't be shy
blocks.t: **Húwag kayóng mahiyâ.** is a very common expression of hosts when they offer food to their guests. It helps the guests feel more welcome in their homes.
Leaving a party and thanking the hosts.

items.en: It is late (at night). Let's go home.

blocks.t: Asking prices and buying at the market. **Magkano** means *how much*.

items.tl: Magkano ang isáng kílo ng baboy?
items.en: How much is a kilo of pork?

items.tl: Bigyán mo akó ng isáng kílo ng baka.
items.en: Give me one kilo of beef.
Is this made in the Philippines?

items.tl: Saán akó makakabilí ng mga subenir?

items.en: This is not the correct change.
The price is fair. (the book's other way to say it)

blocks.title: Book spellings
blocks.t: The market list prints **karne** (meat); the dining-room list prints **karné**.
Describing things in the kitchen and giving kitchen jobs. Most describing sentences use the pattern **describing word + ang + thing**:

blocks.title: describing word + ang + thing
blocks.note: The stove is hot. · The knife is sharp.

items.tl: Hugásan nang mabúti ang mga gúlay.

blocks.t: Phrases for mealtime. Look for the **paki-** request words from Lesson 24: **Pakiabót** (please pass), **Pakidalá** (please bring), **Pakiligpít** (please clear).

items.en: What's for breakfast (or lunch or dinner)?
It is time to eat. (the book's other way to say it)

blocks.title: Ulam
blocks.t: **Ulam** (viand) is the dish that goes with rice at every meal. So **Anó ang ulam?** is how you ask what's for breakfast, lunch or dinner.
Welcoming visitors and chatting with them.

items.en: Please come in and sit down.
We are happy that you came.

items.tl: Ibig ba ninyóng makiníg ng tugtóg?
items.en: Do you wish to listen to some music?

items.tl: Ibig ba ninyóng magbasá ng diyaryo?
items.en: Would you like to read the newspaper?

items.tl: Ibig ba ninyó ng malamíg na túbig?
items.en: Would you like some cold water?

items.tl: Gáano katagál na kayóng nakatirá rito?
items.en: How long have you been living here?

items.tl: Ang mga tao dito ay mabubuti at matutulungin.
items.en: The people here are friendly and helpful.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Polite requests with **paki-**: Pakiabót, Pakidalá, Pakiligpít, Pakibalot.
Host phrases: **Tulóy kayó. Maupô kayó.** **Húwag kayóng mahiyâ.**

exercises.q: How do you ask "May I ask something?"
You want the jeepney to stop at the corner. What do you call out?
exercises.explain: Dirétso lang = Straight ahead; Maghintáy ka rito = Wait here.

exercises.q: Which phrase tells a child "Do not cry"?
exercises.explain: Huwág kayóng mag-away = Don't quarrel; Matúlog ka na = Go to sleep.

exercises.q: "Búkas ay Lúnes." What does it mean?
exercises.explain: Ngayón ay Linggó = Today is Sunday.

exercises.q: How do you say "I do not understand"?
exercises.explain: Hindí kitá kilalá = I do not know you.

exercises.q: What does "Ikínagagalák kong mákilala kayó" mean?
options: I am pleased to meet you.
exercises.answer: I am pleased to meet you.
exercises.explain: A polite phrase when you are introduced.

options: The formal coat and tie introduced by the Americans

exercises.q: A host says "Húwag kayóng mahiyâ." What do they mean?
exercises.explain: A very common expression when hosts offer food to their guests.

exercises.q: Which is another way the book gives to say "Thank you. I am already full"?
exercises.explain: Salámat. Busóg na akó. is the first way.

exercises.q: At the market, how do you say "This is expensive"?

recap: Directions: Puwédeng magtanóng? Saán…? Pára po (sa kánto)! Kánan/Kaliwâ. Dirétso lang.
Children: Halíka. Huwág kang umiyák. Matúlog ka na. Magpakábaít ka.
Learning Tagalog: Hindî ko maintindihán. Paki-úlit nga. Paáno sinásabi sa Tagálog ang ... ?
Introductions: Ang pangalan ko ay… Ikínagagalák kong mákilala kayó.
Guest and host: Tulóy kayó. Kumáin na táyo. Húwag kayóng mahiyâ. Salámat. Busóg na akó.
Market and table: Magkano ito? Pakiabót ng kánin. Ang saráp ng pagkain!
